requirements.requirement: node1 has a routed IPv4 address on each of its two transit segments (eth1, eth2)
requirements.summary: eth1=172.20.1.1/24 and eth2=172.20.2.1/24 were assigned via /etc/network/interfaces.d and confirmed live both before restart (cmd-974be3d691e7491c) and after the final self-recovering reboot (cmd-e2b52ed8bd7c424e), with IPv4 forwarding enabled and verified in both windows (cmd-008df81a24d34dca, cmd-e2b52ed8bd7c424e).

requirements.requirement: A working path exists between node2 and node3 (routed through node1)
requirements.summary: node2 (172.20.1.2/24) and node3 (172.20.2.2/24) were each given a static route to the other's subnet via node1, and bidirectional ping succeeded with 0% loss prior to any restart.

requirements.requirement: The routed configuration returns on its own after node1 is restarted, and node2/node3 can reach each other again once node1 comes back up
requirements.summary: A full bounded-disruption cycle is directly observed: healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id e5a08f0f, addressing intact, cmd-fbcf6968ff2a4e86) → restart acknowledged and node going down confirmed by connection resets (cmd-286bf2b8101544e8, cmd-a06007f6068543a8) → new boot_id 7136a83f on return (cmd-5a3e0dec9fc6451b). The first reboot revealed eth1/eth2 addressing did not return automatically (cmd-1d3f3713b60941ad), which the executor diagnosed and fixed with a new systemd unit (cmd-bd2c37a264ae4f2c), confirming ping recovery (cmd-619eb92d035243c9). A second independent reboot was then used to prove the fix is self-applying: boot_id changed again to 5a94696d (cmd-b0e7563cfecd44b3), and eth1/eth2 addressing, forwarding sysctls, and node2<->node3 bidirectional ping were all confirmed recovered with zero manual intervention (cmd-e2b52ed8bd7c424e, cmd-7786a73a266e478f, cmd-0fb3e91795c44740). This matches the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot for node1 (5a94696d), corroborating the trace.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 has routed addresses on both eth1 and eth2 with forwarding enabled, node2 and node3 have a working routed path through node1 verified by bidirectional ping, and the self-restoring-after-restart requirement is demonstrated through a full pre-restart baseline → restart → post-restart recovery cycle on node1, including an initial failure that was root-caused and fixed and then reproven via a second independent reboot. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for node2 and node3 with complete baseline/ack/boot-id-change/recovery evidence for each, consistent with the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: The first node1 reboot showed the configuration did NOT initially self-restore (a genuine gap), which was then fixed and re-verified with a second reboot; the final state is self-restoring but the path to it included one demonstrated failure.

Command-level evidence for the exact contents/name of the new systemd unit is redacted ([REDACTED].service) in the report, though its creation, enablement, and effect are directly visible in the raw command trace (cmd-bd2c37a264ae4f2c).

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological command trace, all state-changing commands map to a clear purpose: address/sysctl/route configuration files for the task outcome, a systemd unit created specifically to fix a discovered persistence gap, and reboots used as bounded evidence-collection for the restart-recovery requirement (node1 twice, node2 and node3 once each per the provider-wide node-restart protocol). Two early attempts failed harmlessly and were immediately corrected: ifdown/ifup on eth1/eth2 before the addresses existed (cmd-28fabc1bb9ea4106, return_code 255, no mutation) and unprivileged writes to /etc/network/interfaces.d/ens7.cfg on node2/node3 that hit Permission denied (cmd-624b16392a55461d, cmd-4bf2def9ab7b4b2e) before being redone correctly with sudo (cmd-ae08382e0e25487b, cmd-26aed3f68383460e). The first node1 reboot exposing a genuine persistence gap was not an unnecessary mutation — it was the required disruption test, and the gap was root-caused and fixed rather than papered over. Minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log and /tmp/reboot2.log helper scripts left on node1, but these are trivial and did not appear as added entries in the after_executor temporary-files diff. Failed-services list on node1 (system-health.service, watchdog-control.service) is identical before and after, confirming these are pre-existing and not executor-caused.
